domain: Transportation Systems / Institutional Coordination / Path Dependency
topic_summary: Analysis of the convention determining which side of the road vehicles drive on, examining the coordination mechanisms, historical path dependencies, and structural constraints that maintain right-hand versus left-hand driving systems across different jurisdictions.

key_tensions: Network coordination benefits vs switching costs
National sovereignty vs regional harmonization pressure
key_mechanisms: Legal enforcement (traffic laws mandate side choice)
Vehicle design lock-in (steering wheel position, control placement)
Infrastructure investment path dependency (road geometry, intersection design)
absences: Safety outcome data comparing left vs right systems
Economic analysis of switching costs vs coordination benefits

axes.structural_delta: Once a side is chosen, network effects create self-reinforcing coordination that makes unilateral switching prohibitively costly
axes.primary_observable: Switching cost estimates (infrastructure, vehicle fleet, retraining); adoption rate stability over time
axes.selection_reason: Foundational coordination constraint; upstream to all other axes; mountain providing physical/economic base

axes.structural_delta: Current side choice reflects colonial power's historical imposition rather than independent optimization
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between former colonial status and side choice; timing of adoption relative to independence
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (historical correlation vs network economics); different beneficiary structure; piton hypothesis captures atrophied sovereignty

axes.structural_delta: Jurisdictions with neighbors using opposite side bear coordination costs (accidents, delays, vehicle modifications) that isolated jurisdictions avoid
axes.primary_observable: Border-crossing accident rates; vehicle modification requirements; traffic delay metrics at side-mismatched borders
axes.selection_reason: Different observable (border-specific costs vs general network effects); distinct victim set; rope captures coordination failure between systems

axes.structural_delta: Global vehicle manufacturing optimizes for dominant right-hand market, imposing cost premiums on left-hand jurisdictions
axes.primary_observable: Price differentials for right-hand-drive vehicles; model availability in left-hand markets; manufacturing plant specialization
axes.selection_reason: Different observable (manufacturing economics vs coordination costs); distinct beneficiary/victim structure; tangled_rope captures market power extraction

axes.structural_delta: No measurable safety difference between left and right systems when controlling for infrastructure quality and enforcement
axes.primary_observable: Accident rate comparisons controlling for GDP, road quality, enforcement; within-country switching studies (Sweden 1967)
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: absence of data (extraction_summary notes missing safety comparisons); would require empirical grounding not present in topic; omega variable

deferred_axes.structural_delta: No measurable safety difference between systems
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Insufficient empirical data in source material; extraction_summary notes absence of safety outcome comparisons; requires domain-specific research to validate mountain classification

omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + F03 concern

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: coordination_equilibrium classified as mountain based on historical switching costs, but modern technology (digital infrastructure, modular manufacturing) may have reduced switching costs enough to reclassify as piton. Generated omega_switching_feasibility to bound this uncertainty. No tunnel vision: axes drawn from coordination theory, historical sociology, manufacturing economics, and border studies.
